name: Hanging pawns (Black pair on c5 and d5)

plans.label: Advance the pair
plans.description: The pair's dynamic life: push the d-pawn with piece support to open lines and plant a wedge before the pawns become targets.

success.note: The pair advanced intact: the d-pawn stands on d4 with the c-pawn still beside it.

plans.label: Use the flanking files
plans.description: Put rooks on the half-open b- and e-files the pair's birth opened, so the pawns are a spearhead and not only a liability.

success.note: A Black rook on the b-file and a Black rook on the e-file — the two flanking files the pair's birth opened. The plan names the squares, so the census is literal. It counts placement, not what the placement is worth.

plans.label: Queens on while the pair stands
plans.description: The pair lives on piece energy: keep the queens on the board while the pawns still stand on c5 and d5.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Keep pieces on', whose success was what the avoided trades were worth. It is now the state the plan is defending: the pair still stands on c5 and d5 and both queens are still on the board. Queens are the piece the plan is really about; the minor pieces are not counted. Original success note: 'Detection cannot count what a trade was worth.'

plans.label: Provoke and degrade
plans.description: Pile on the pawns, provoke an advance, blockade the square the advance left behind, and win the straggler.

success.note: The pair degraded: one pawn fell or was traded off, leaving the survivor isolated.

plans.label: Queens off with the pair still fixed
plans.description: Exchange the queens that give the pair its dynamism and leave the pawns on c5 and d5 as something to attack.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Trade the active pieces', whose success was what the trades were worth. It is now the exact opposite state of the plan it opposes: the queens are off and the pair is still sitting on c5 and d5, a static target. Original success note: 'Detection cannot count what a trade was worth.'

watch: The attacker and defender counts on d4, the square the pair most wants to cross.
Whether each pawn still has its partner beside it.
Who controls the blockading squares c4 and d4 if a pawn advances.
typicalMistakes: Advancing one pawn to win a tempo and leaving the pair split.
Trading the pieces that made the pawns dynamic, then defending them forever.
Besieging the pawns head-on while the supported advance is still available.
